newsitem.title: USA: Asarco net cut by lower copper prices.
newsitem.headline: Asarco net cut by lower copper prices.

text.p: Asarco Inc Thursday reported a drop in third quarter earnings to $6.0 million from $58.3 million a year earlier saying the decline in the copper price over the past year is estimated to have reduced the company's net earnings by about $67 million in the quarter.
Improvements in operations and price increases of other metals Asarco produces offset a portion of this decline.
Commenting on the outlook for the balance of 1996 and 1997, Chairman Richard de J. Osborne said, "The fundamentals of the copper market are good and getting better.
"Production from new mines is being absorbed by rising consumption and inventories in commodity exchange warehouses are declining rapidly," Osborne explained.

"This improvement is not yet reflected in the price of copper, which seems more affected by perception than by fundamentals at the present time. The market is not yet free from the uncertainties created by the trading losses of one large market participant," he said.
The company said its copper price protection program resulted in a pretax third quarter gain of $13.7 million on the sale or exercise of puts covering 73,000 tons of copper.

At September 30, Asarco had remaining price protection covering 41,000 tons of copper and Southern Peru Copper Corp had remaining price protection covering 40,000 tons of copper for the fourth quarter of 1996 and first quarter of 1997. The put options have an average strike price of $1.02 per pound for Asarco and $0.95 per pound for SPCC.

In addition, Asarco said, it has realized pretax gains of $24.4 million from the sale of copper put options which will be recognized in the fourth quarter of 1996 and in 1997 when the underlying production is sold.

Asarco said its beneficial interest in mined copper production in the latest quarter was 251.3 million pounds compared with 226.4 million pounds in the year earlier period, representing an increase of 11.0 percent.

Sales of products and services were $647.8 million in the latest quarter, compared with $819.7 million 1995's third quarter, it reported, saying the decline was principally a result of lower copper prices.
The average price for copper on the New York Commodity Exchange (COMEX) in the third quarter of 1996 was $0.91 per pound compared with $1.36 in the third quarter of 1995.
The average London Metal Exchange (LME) copper price was $0.90 compared with $1.37 in the year-earlier period.
Asarco said about 48 percent of its consolidated copper sales in the third quarter were based on the COMEX price with the balance based on LME quotations.

The average LME price for lead was $0.36 per pound compared with $0.28 in the third quarter of 1995. The average zinc price was $0.45 per pound compared with $0.46 in the year earlier period. The molybdenum price averaged $3.29 per pound in the third quarter of 1996 compared with $4.37 a year ago. The average price for silver was $5.05 per ounce compared with $5.33 in the third quarter of 1995.
